notes: Positions only: every byte comes from the user's own ROM at extraction time.

Program data (the data area 0x100000-0x17FFFF and what the code chips hold besides the code, 0x000000-0x01FFFF and 0x080000-0x09FFFF): text files by subject (system/, video/, engine/, objects/, player/, stages/, scenes/), a section a piece, cut where symbols.txt names a place, in the format data_formats.json gives it; the code and the chips' mirrors are left out (the C replaces the code, and the game's assets pack holds none of it), except the bytes of the code the game also reads as data ('read_as_data': where, how many and why); layout.json lists the pieces in order.

Sprites: every frame of sprite_frame_records (program ROM 0x130000) in sprite sheets, an animation family or an object a sheet, in folders by subject (sprite_sheets.txt: sonic/walking, stage_08/lava_flow, title/sega_logo...): an indexed PNG each, with the palettes the frames are drawn with (sprite_palettes.json: positions in the program ROM), and a JSON beside it that says where each frame is in the sheet and where it goes back in the sprite ROM; pen 0 is transparent.

Tile sheets are 8-bit indexed PNGs in color: the 16 palettes the sheet's tiles are shown with the most (tile_palettes.json, positions in the program ROM), a tile's pixels at its palette's slot * 16 + pen, so index & 15 is the pen; pen 0 is transparent. Each sheet's JSON says every tile's palette.

Sound program (epr-15785, the first 0x40000 bytes of the sound region; the board repeats it four times): its data as text files, cut where sound_symbols.txt names a place, in the format sound_formats.json gives it; its code is left out (the C replaces it); its jump table is data (the driver reads it before it jumps). layout.json lists the pieces in order. The songs (the banked part from 0x010000, 'movable') may change size: the build lays them out one after another and the song records find them by name.

PCM samples (0x100000-0x3FFFFF of the sound region): one 8-bit WAV a sample of pcm_sample_headers (sound program 0x6429, 175 of them), one ROM byte a WAV sample, so they go back exactly; samples.json says where each goes. The rate is nominal (half the RF5C68 output rate): the driver sets the pitch of every note.

read_as_data.name: program_start_read_as_data
read_as_data.why: the program's first 512 bytes, up to the boot values (and program_start_read_as_data_2 after them): what a null pointer reads, as a structure (as large as struct player), as the text of a queue slot with no text (draw_queued_strings; the second byte ends it) or as the trail of a stage with none (start_map_trail: 0xFFFFFFFF, its points from 000001)

read_as_data.name: program_start_read_as_data_2
read_as_data.why: the rest of the program's first 512 bytes, after the boot values (program_start_read_as_data)

read_as_data.name: code_below_bridge_sag_curve
read_as_data.why: compute_bridge_sag's curve index for a loaded plank past the bridge's middle is 16 bits: a negative one (-255 to -1) reads 64 KB up from bridge_sag_curve

read_as_data.name: code_past_text_frames
read_as_data.why: draw_queued_strings' sprite frame for a character code 80-FF (as the text at a null pointer has): text_frames has 128, so it reads up to 256 bytes past it, in start_ranking_entry's code

read_as_data.name: title_code_read_as_marker
read_as_data.why: map_screen_update's icon target for a stage with no marker (stage_map_markers FF): map_stage_positions[FF], past the table, in the title's code
